translationRepairs: At that time the Prince of Pingnan, Shang Kexi, and the Prince of Jingnan, Geng Jizhuo, both held Guangdong. Yongjian listed eight abuses there: too many petty agents, too many surcharges, village labor service without fixed rules, corvée without fixed quotas, salt franchises growing more oppressive by the day, illicit levies swelling daily, and rampant logging and fuel-cutting—all of which should be abolished at once.

At that time the Prince of Pingnan, Shang Kexi, and the Prince of Jingnan, Geng Jimao, both held Guangdong. Yongjian listed eight abuses there: too many petty agents, too many surcharges, village labor service without fixed rules, corvée without fixed quotas, salt franchises growing more oppressive by the day, illicit levies swelling daily, and rampant logging and fuel-cutting—all of which should be abolished at once.
s0018 names 靖南王耿繼茂; 繼茂 romanizes as Jimao, not Jizhuo. The proposed name correction is accurate and leaves the rest of the idiomatic sentence intact.

At the time the Prince of Pingnan Shang Kexi and the Prince of Jingnan Geng Jizhuo both garrisoned Guangdong; Yongjian memorialized eight policies in Guangdong that harmed the people: delegated clerks too numerous, miscellaneous levies too many, village corvée without fixed rules, labor requisition without fixed regulations, salt monopolies growing daily overbearing, private taxes daily increasing, cutting firewood and gathering timber spreading great harm—all should urgently be abolished.

At the time the Prince of Pingnan Shang Kexi and the Prince of Jingnan Geng Jimao both garrisoned Guangdong; Yongjian memorialized eight policies in Guangdong that harmed the people: delegated clerks too numerous, miscellaneous levies too many, village corvée without fixed rules, labor requisition without fixed regulations, salt monopolies growing daily overbearing, private taxes daily increasing, cutting firewood and gathering timber spreading great harm—all should urgently be abolished.
The literal likewise misreads 耿繼茂 as Geng Jizhuo; Geng Jimao restores the correct personal name while preserving the rest of the sentence.
The court soon ordered Geng Jizhuo to move his headquarters to Fujian, a change Yongjian had initiated.
The court soon ordered Geng Jimao to move his headquarters to Fujian, a change Yongjian had initiated.
s0021’s 繼茂 resumes the same Prince of Jingnan named 耿繼茂 in s0018; Jimao is correct and Jizhuo is not.
He earned his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Shunzhi and was posted as investigating censor for Chengdu Prefecture in Sichuan.
He earned his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Shunzhi and was posted as prefectural judge of Chengdu Prefecture in Sichuan.
s0056 has 授四川成都府推官; 推官 is a prefectural judicial post (prefectural judge), not an investigating censor (御史).
In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed investigating censor of Chengdu Prefecture in Sichuan.
In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed prefectural judge of Chengdu Prefecture in Sichuan.
The literal also renders 推官 as investigating censor; prefectural judge of Chengdu Prefecture correctly translates 成都府推官.
Diyu had won a good name years before as investigating censor, and the people were glad to see him return.
Diyu had won a good name years before as prefectural judge, and the people were glad to see him return.
s0099 has 先為推官有聲, referring back to the Chengdu 推官 post, not a censorial office; prefectural judge is correct.
Diyu had earlier been famous as investigating censor, and the common people rejoiced at his coming.
Diyu had earlier been famous as prefectural judge, and the common people rejoiced at his coming.
The literal repeats the same office error for 推官; prefectural judge matches the Chinese.
Bringing back one eminent family can do as much as several hundred common households.
Bringing back one eminent family can do as much as several common households.
s0104’s 百姓數戶 is several common households, not several hundred; the proposal correctly drops 'hundred' but needlessly omits 百姓 ('common'), which the original phrasing already captured.
Junior Guardian Shao Yuanping wrote that 'southerners are flighty and unfit for office.'
Vice Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent Shao Yuanping wrote that 'southerners are flighty and unfit for office.'
s0140 titles Shao 少詹事, the vice supervisor of the heir apparent’s household; Junior Guardian would be 少保 and is the wrong office.
He became vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and rose to its minister.
He became vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and rose to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
s0174 has 授光祿寺少卿，累遷太常寺卿: 光祿寺 is the Court of Imperial Entertainments and 太常寺 the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the original wrongly treats both as Sacrifices.
Song Luo, whose courtesy name was Muqiong, came from Shangqiu in Henan and was the son of Quan.
Song Luo, whose courtesy name was Muzhong, came from Shangqiu in Henan and was the son of Quan.
s0201 gives the courtesy name 牧仲; 牧仲 is Muzhong, not Muqiong.
Song Luo, courtesy name Muqiong, was a native of Shangqiu in Henan and son of Quan.
Song Luo, courtesy name Muzhong, was a native of Shangqiu in Henan and son of Quan.
The literal likewise misreads 牧仲 as Muqiong; Muzhong restores the correct courtesy-name reading.
This uses the old idea of turning the Huai against the Yellow.
This uses the unchanging principle of turning the Huai against the Yellow.
s0243’s 不易之理 is an unchanging/immutable principle of 淮敵黃; 'old idea' understates 不易 and is not an accurate rendering.
This borrows the principle that the Huai is hard to pit against the Yellow.
This borrows the unchanging principle of pitting the Huai against the Yellow.
The literal misreads 不易 as 'not easy' and flips 淮敵黃 into difficulty pitting Huai against Yellow; the proposed unchanging principle of pitting the Huai against the Yellow matches the Chinese.
In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to Huguang.
In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to Hubei.
s0259 has 調湖北; 湖北 is Hubei, whereas Huguang is 湖廣—a different toponym.
In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to Huguang.
In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to Hubei.
The literal repeats the same toponym error; Hubei correctly translates 湖北.
Yongjian in Guizhou, Diyu in Sichuan, Hongzuo in Guangdong, Zhi in Jiangxi, Luo following Zhi, and Shen carrying on Yongjian's work—all labored hard to restore order after the war.
Yongjian in Guizhou, Diyu in Sichuan, Hongzuo in Guangdong, Zhi in Jiangxi, Luo following Zhi, and Shen distantly continuing Yongjian—all labored hard to restore order after the war.
s0270 has 詵遙繼雍建; 遙繼 marks distant/remote succession, which 'carrying on Yongjian's work' omits. The proposed 'distantly continuing Yongjian' restores that sense.
